target_customer: Mid size and large companies in Latin America (Rappi, Olist, Addi) that sell and support customers over WhatsApp
problem: Companies want to reach customers through WhatsApp at scale for marketing and support without building a call center, and WhatsApp limits automation without an approved provider.
business_model: B2B SaaS and messaging platform, usage and subscription based

prior_employers: A grocery delivery company (unnamed), customer experience team, 2018

technical_complexity.rationale: Building on the WhatsApp Business API with campaign tooling, analytics and later AI conversation handling is standard engineering with platform approval hurdles.

defensibility.rationale: Depends on WhatsApp access and customer integrations; many messaging providers can offer similar tooling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented. Twilio Ventures invested in the 2022 round rather than competing directly in coverage found.

market_need_then: WhatsApp was the dominant messaging channel across Latin America; the founders prototyped text message surveys at a delivery company in 2018 and saw fast internal adoption.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional business press coverage exists, but no sourced brand assets, community or name story.

pivots.from: Text message surveys for customer feedback
pivots.to: WhatsApp conversations for marketing and customer service
pivots.why: The survey prototype spread to other teams, then the founders focused on WhatsApp (El Espectador interview as summarized by search).

outcome_analysis: Treble.ai grew with WhatsApp's dominance in Latin America, serving hundreds of companies and automating over 70 million conversations by 2022, which supported a 15 million dollar Series A led by Tiger Global. It remains active; later rounds were not found, and WhatsApp platform dependency is the main structural risk.
